summary: This diff fixes a real, verifiable bug in the Excel BoQ importer's header-mapping logic (construction-boq-import-service.ts): mapBoqHeaders previously picked the first header in sheet order matching any alias, which meant a generic 'Category' column could be chosen as the description field ahead of a more specific 'Description (Task)' column, and 'Sl No' was missing entirely from the itemCode alias list. The fix changes header resolution to try each field's aliases in priority order (verified correct by manual trace against the new test fixture: 'Sl No' -> itemCode, 'Description (Task)' -> description, 'Sub Task' -> subTask), adds a new subTask column concept with description fallback for unlabeled sub-task rows, and adds positional parent-child inference (attaching a description-less, breakdown%-bearing row to the itemCode of the nearest preceding row) that correctly resets at each new parent task in the traced example. The change is scoped entirely to construction-boq-import-service.ts + its test file, does not touch computeHierarchicalAmount() or the DB layer, and the only downstream consumer (src/app/api/construction/boq/import/route.ts) only reads lineItems/warnings/totalRows from parseBoqSpreadsheet's output, which is unaffected. PROGRESS.md and ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml updates are documentation/coordination only. No .github/workflows/**, migrations, schema, auth, permission, payment, billing, rls, or .env files are touched, matching the deterministic tier1 classification. I could not execute `bun test` in this review environment (bun binary not present) so the worker's own reported '6 pass, 0 fail' could not be independently re-run, but I hand-traced the new test's exact fixture through mapBoqHeaders and mapRowsToLineItems line-by-line and every assertion in the new test holds given the actual code.

The positional sub-task-to-parent inference (attach to 'nearest preceding row with an itemCode' when a row has no description but does have a Sub Task value and a breakdown %) is a heuristic tailored to this specific two-level BoQ shape; it has not been proven against deeper/irregular hierarchies (e.g. sub-tasks with their own sub-tasks, or breakdown% present on non-subtask rows), though this is a scoped, well-documented limitation and not a defect in the shipped change.
